title: Course Configuration
description: Runtime config for course-specific content loaded by ta-chat.mjs

abbreviations.description: Map of abbreviation to expansion (e.g. {"gdp": "gross domestic product"}). Merged on top of built-in French lecture synonyms.

academic_signals.description: Course-specific terms/stems for academic signal detection. Combined with ~60 built-in generic academic terms.

terminology_fr.description: French terminology table appended to French responses. Empty string or omit for no suffix.

course_topics.description: Chapter/session labels (e.g. ["S1: Introduction", "S2: Core Concepts"]). Metadata only.

question_type_labels.description: Optional display labels for exercise type codes, e.g. {"STATA": {"fr": "Logiciel", "en": "Software"}}.

hidden_question_types.description: Type codes to exclude from the quiz UI entirely (e.g. ["STATA"]). Exercises remain in data but are never shown to students.

features.description: Feature flags read by the backend at cold-start.

auth_required.description: Set to false to disable password login. Useful for demos. Rate limiting still applies.

quiz_mode_enabled.description: Show the quiz mode toggle in the UI. Defaults to true if exercises exist, false otherwise.

prompt_profile.description: Which system-prompt persona the assistant adopts. 'course_ta' = university-level teaching assistant with short conversational prose, source-grounded answers, and hints before homework solutions. 'content_companion' = guide grounded in the supplied content for paper/book/manual companions. Defaults to 'course_ta' for backwards compatibility.

assistant_persona.description: Free-text addendum appended to the system prompt — describes who the assistant is and the audience. E.g. 'You are a companion to a research paper on minimum-wage effects; readers are policy analysts.'
